To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
in mice with growth-hormone receptor deletion in liver, the expression of key regulators for mitochondrial biogenesis in the brain and kidneys is sex dependent.
the expression of genes involved in mitochondrial biogenesis is sexually dimorphic and that the liver is the main organ responsible for the regulation of the GH/IGF-1 axis.
the gene expression of regulators of mitochondrial biogeneration is sex dependent in LiGHRKO mice.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a novel aspect of mitochondrial biology in the LiGHRKO mice.
the role of the sex-dependent regulation of key regulators of mitochondria biogenesis in LiGHRKO mice.
the role of sex hormones in the regulation of gene expression of key factors of mitochondrial biogenesis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the expression of the genes involved in mitochondrial biogenesis is different between male and female mice, but only in the brain.
the gene expression of mitochondrial biogenesis regulators is sex-dependent in the brains and kidneys of LiGHRKO mice.
the sex-specific differences in gene expression of key factors of mitochondrial biogenesis are not associated with LiGHRKO.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
LiGHRKO mice have a different expression of key regulators and a marker of mitochondria in brain, kidney and liver compared to wild-type mice.
the LiGHRKO mice have a sex-dependent regulation of mitochondrial biogenesis.
LiGHRKO female mice have lower levels of Pgc1a, Ampk and Sift1 in the brain and kidneys compared to males.
The main takeaway from our work is that
sex-dependent gene expression of key mitochondrial regulators is a common feature in mice with Ghr gene deletion in the liver.
sex differences in the regulation of mitochondrial biogenesis are tissue-specific and that the regulation is different in LiGHRKO mice compared to GHRKO mice.
the gene expression of the key regulators of mitochondrial function is sex dependent.
